CONFIRMED (real run 2026-10-06, 2 videos, commentsPerPost=50): the default dataset holds VIDEO items, not comments. Each item carries commentsDatasetUrl, a separate dataset shared by all videos of that run. `work` now fetches it (ApifyProvider.iterItemsFromUrl, CommentIngestor) and maps items into pipeline.comment by the numeric id parsed from submittedVideoUrl/videoWebUrl; a comment for a video not in pipeline.video is skipped, not fatal. Reads from that sub-dataset are billed as Apify storage-operation reads (~$0.0004/1000), separate from and far smaller than the run's own pay-per-event cost.

The schema says the actual comment count may differ from commentsPerPost. First real run (commentsPerPost=50, no maxRepliesPerComment) returned zero reply items even though replyCommentTotal > 0 on top-level comments -- so maxRepliesPerComment=5 was added (2026-10-06) to actually fetch some, as a small test. Per Apify's own actor docs: topLevelCommentsPerPost 'only applies to profile searches' (we use postURLs, so it would be a no-op -- left out); maxRepliesPerComment caps replies per top-level comment, same pay-per-event pricing as any other item, so it is NOT free and scales with how many comments actually have replies.
Per-run total cap = maxTotalChargeUsd + query param maxItems (may not apply to this pay-per-event actor); the video list is already truncated by pipeline.comments.total-items-cap / per-video-cap.
